sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier: head in dorsal view nearly black or dark chestnut brown on the anterior 1/3, the frontal margin the darkest structure, the posterior 2/3 rusty orange; outline of the anterior margin of the frontal margin bracket-shaped; head capsule sculpture dense, fine and undulating (which the specific name refers to); frontal face deeply and evenly concave, meeting the vertex face at almost 90° in frontal view; frontal margin narrow, with a median notch, delimited from the vertex by a median swelling; frontal horns fused with the frontal margin, bluntly conical; genal horns small and warty, about 1/10 the volume of the frontal horns. Alate: pale brown, head oval with distinct cranial sutures, antennae 14—16-segmented, mostly 14 or 15; transverse band and midline of the pronotum distinct. Colour pattern similar to that of C. rotundiceps, but the latter has larger compound eyes and ocelli and a greater body length (including the wings), and its head is nearly circular rather than elongate in dorsal view.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body pale brown. Sclerotized veins pale brown, the wing membrane pale smoky brown. Chevron mark on the wing scale pale brown, weakly delimited. Labrum, frontal face, antennae and pronotum very pale brown. Vertex and abdominal tergites pale brown. Sternites pale yellow-brown. Femora nearly white, the legs including the ends of the tibiae very pale brown. Head oval, the cranial sutures distinct. Compound eyes medium-sized, oval. Ocelli rather small, oval, touching the compound eyes. Antennae 14—16-segmented, mostly 14 or 15, the segment formula variable. Pronotum subsquare, narrower than the head width (including the compound eyes); anterior margin shallowly concave, the sides slightly convex, posterior margin slightly concave; transverse band and midline distinct. Media of the forewing reaching 1/3 of the wing length; radial sector with 5—6 branches. Arolia distinct.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Vertex in dorsal view nearly black or dark chestnut brown on the anterior 1/3, the frontal margin the darkest structure, the posterior 2/3 rusty orange; in lateral view the anterior 1/3 of the head black or dark chestnut brown, grading to rusty orange over the posterior 2/3. Mandibles dark chestnut brown. Anterior margin of the pronotum rusty with a pouch-like internal process, the remainder yellow-white. Anterior outline of the frontal margin bracket-shaped in dorsal view; the sides of the head slightly constricted behind the frontal margin and swollen posteriorly. Anterior half of the head (dorsal view) distinctly sculptured; sculpture dense, fine and undulating. Anterior 1/3 of the vertex with a small median concavity. Frontal margin narrow, sculptured, with a median notch, clearly delimited from the vertex by a median swelling. Frontal face deeply and evenly concave. In frontal view the laterally extended part of the frontal face makes an angle of about 90° with the vertex face. Labrum pointed, distinctly swollen at the apex. Frontal horns fused with the frontal margin, bluntly conical, sculptured. Genal horns warty and small, hidden by the frontal horns in dorsal view; their volume about 1/10 that of the frontal horns. Genal horns separate from the frontal horns. Mandibles swollen and distinctly angled at the base, falcate behind the swelling, of medium length; the first marginal tooth of both mandibles distinct. Compound eyes small but distinct, oval. Antennae 11—14-segmented, mostly 11 or 14, the segment formula variable, often 2>3=4=5 or 2>3<4=5. Pronotum shield-shaped, subsquare, the anterior margin notched and biconvex, the sides almost parallel and slightly converging posteriorly; anterior margin with a shallow, dense undulate rim; posterior margin slightly concave. Comparison with C. mangoldi: in the latter the head capsule sculpture is shallower and the frontal margin broader.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Distribution: Puerto Rico, Greater Antilles, widespread from coastal to inland forest habitats but uncommon, accounting for 7% of the Puerto Rican collections of drywood termites. Type locality: 2 km east of Recio on Highway 3, Puerto Rico.
